\chapter{Communication Complexity — Hamming}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.Hamming
\section{Overview}

This module develops the combinatorics of Hamming balls and spheres over a finite alphabet
$\alpha$ of size $q$.  The main results are exact cardinality formulas: the Hamming sphere
of radius $k$ centred at any word has size $\binom{n}{k}(q-1)^k$, and the Hamming ball of
radius $r$ has size $\mathrm{ballVol}(n,r,q) = \sum_{i=0}^{r}\binom{n}{i}(q-1)^i$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Word]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Word}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Word}
\leanok
A \emph{word} of length $n$ over alphabet $\alpha$ is a function
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \alpha$; it is an abbreviation for the type of
length-$n$ codewords used throughout this module.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hamming ball]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.hammingBall}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.hammingBall}
\leanok
\statementsource{ada-coding-book}{pdf-7251cb8e4bc5-p029-b006}
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word}
The \emph{Hamming ball} of radius $r$ centred at $u \in \alpha^n$ is the finset
\[
  B_r(u) = \{v \in \alpha^n : \mathrm{hammingDist}(u,v) \le r\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hamming sphere]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word}
The \emph{Hamming sphere} of radius $r$ centred at $u \in \alpha^n$ is the finset
\[
  S_r(u) = \{v \in \alpha^n : \mathrm{hammingDist}(u,v) = r\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Ball volume]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.ballVol}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.ballVol}
\leanok
\statementsource{ada-coding-book}{pdf-7251cb8e4bc5-p070-b003}
For a length-$n$ code over an alphabet of size $q$, the \emph{ball volume} at radius $t$ is
\[
  \mathrm{ballVol}(n,t,q) = \sum_{i=0}^{t} \binom{n}{i}(q-1)^i \in \mathbb{N}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Disjointness of Hamming spheres of distinct radii]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSpheres_disjoint}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSpheres_disjoint}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, fix a centre word $u \in \alpha^n$, and let $r$ and
$t$ be natural numbers with $r \ne t$. Then the Hamming sphere $S_r(u) = \{v \in
\alpha^n : d(u,v) = r\}$ of radius $r$ and the Hamming sphere $S_t(u) = \{v \in \alpha^n
: d(u,v) = t\}$ of radius $t$, both centred at $u$, are disjoint, where $d$ denotes the
Hamming distance.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Pairwise disjointness of Hamming spheres]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSpheres_pairwise_disjoint}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSpheres_pairwise_disjoint}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere, CommunicationComplexity.hammingSpheres_disjoint}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, let $u \in \alpha^n$ be a word of length $n$, and let
$r$ be a natural number. For $t \in \bbn$, write $S_t(u)$ for the Hamming sphere of
radius $t$ centred at $u$. Then the family $\{S_t(u)\}_{t \in \{0,1,\ldots,r-1\}}$ is
pairwise disjoint: for any two distinct indices $s, t$ with $s, t < r$, the spheres
$S_s(u)$ and $S_t(u)$ share no common word.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hamming ball as the disjoint union of spheres]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.hammingBall_eq_hammingSpheres}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.hammingBall_eq_hammingSpheres}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.hammingBall, CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere, CommunicationComplexity.hammingSpheres_pairwise_disjoint}
\difficulty{3}
Let $u \in \alpha^n$ be a word of length $n$ over a finite alphabet $\alpha$, and let
$r$ be a natural number. Then the Hamming ball of radius $r$ centred at $u$ is the
disjoint union of the Hamming spheres of radii $0, 1, \dots, r$ centred at $u$:
\[
  B_r(u) = \bigsqcup_{k=0}^{r} S_k(u).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Support of a pair of words]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.support}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.support}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word}
The \emph{support} of $v$ relative to $u$ is the finset of coordinate positions
where the two words differ:
$\mathrm{support}(u,v) = \{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n : u_i \ne v_i\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Hamming distance as the size of the support]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.support_dist}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.support_dist}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.support}
\difficulty{1}
Let $u,v$ be words of length $n$ over a finite alphabet $\alpha$, that is, functions
$\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \alpha$. Then the Hamming distance between them equals the number
of coordinates on which they differ:
\[
d(u,v) = \abs{\{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n : u_i \ne v_i\}}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Support fiber]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.support}
For a word $u$ and a finset $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the \emph{support fiber}
is the set of words that differ from $u$ at exactly the positions in $S$:
$\mathrm{supportFiber}(u,S) = \{v : \mathrm{support}(u,v) = S\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Disjointness of support fibers over distinct sets]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber_disjoint}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber_disjoint}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.support, CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber}
\difficulty{2}
Fix a word $u$ of length $n$ over a finite alphabet, and let $S$ and $T$ be two distinct
sets of coordinate positions in $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$. Then the support fiber of $u$ over
$S$ and the support fiber of $u$ over $T$ are disjoint: no word $v$ can differ from $u$
at exactly the positions in $S$ while also differing from $u$ at exactly the positions
in $T$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hamming sphere as a union of support fibers]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere_eq_biUnion}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere_eq_biUnion}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.hammingSphere, CommunicationComplexity.support, CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, let $u \in \alpha^n$ be a word of length $n$, and let
$r$ be a natural number. Then the Hamming sphere $S_r(u)$ of radius $r$ centred at $u$
is the union, taken over all $r$-element subsets $S$ of the $n$ coordinate positions, of
the support fibers of $u$ over $S$ — that is, the sets of words differing from $u$ at
exactly the positions in $S$:
\[
S_r(u) = \bigcup_{\substack{S \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\} \\ \abs{S} = r}} \{\, v \in
\alpha^n : v \text{ and } u \text{ differ in exactly the positions of } S \,\}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Alternative symbol choices]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.choices}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.choices}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word}
For a word $u$ and position $i$, the \emph{choices} at $i$ is the finset of symbols
$a \in \alpha$ with $a \ne u_i$, i.e.\ the non-trivial alternatives for position $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Number of alternative symbols at a position]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.choices_card}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.choices_card}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.choices}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, let $u \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \alpha$ be a word
of length $n$ over $\alpha$, and let $i$ be a position. Then the set of symbols $a \in
\alpha$ with $a \ne u_i$ has cardinality $\abs{\alpha} - 1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Partitioning a support fiber by the symbol at one coordinate]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.choices_partition_supportFiber}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.choices_partition_supportFiber}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.choices, CommunicationComplexity.support, CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, and let $u$ be a word of length $n$ over $\alpha$,
that is, a function $u \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \alpha$. Fix a set $S \subseteq
\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ of coordinate positions together with a further position $i \in
\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and let $F$ be the support fiber of $u$ over $\{i\} \cup S$, namely
the set of words that differ from $u$ in exactly the positions belonging to $\{i\} \cup
S$. Since $i$ lies in $\{i\} \cup S$, every word in $F$ carries at position $i$ some
symbol distinct from $u_i$, and grouping the words of $F$ by that symbol partitions $F$:
it equals the disjoint union, taken over all symbols $a \in \alpha$ with $a \ne u_i$, of
the sets $\{v \in F : v_i = a\}$,
\[
  F = \bigsqcup_{\substack{a \in \alpha \\ a \ne u_i}} \{\, v \in F : v_i = a \,\}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Support fibers split into equal-cardinality slices]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.piece_card}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.piece_card}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.choices, CommunicationComplexity.support, CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber}
\difficulty{6}
Let $u$ be a word of length $n$ over a finite alphabet $\alpha$, let $S$ be a set of
coordinate positions, and let $i$ be a position with $i \notin S$. For every symbol $a
\in \alpha$ with $a \ne u_i$, the words in the support fiber of $u$ over $\{i\} \cup S$
— those differing from $u$ at exactly the positions in $\{i\} \cup S$ — whose entry at
position $i$ equals $a$ are exactly as many as the words in the support fiber of $u$
over $S$, that is, the words differing from $u$ at exactly the positions in $S$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality of a support fiber]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.card_supportFiber}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.card_supportFiber}
\leanok
\proofsource{ada-coding-book}{pdf-7251cb8e4bc5-p032-b001}
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Word, CommunicationComplexity.choices_card, CommunicationComplexity.choices_partition_supportFiber, CommunicationComplexity.piece_card, CommunicationComplexity.support, CommunicationComplexity.supportFiber}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, fix a word $u \colon \{1,\dots,n\} \to \alpha$ of
length $n$, and let $S \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}$ be a set of coordinate positions. Then
the number of words $v$ of length $n$ over $\alpha$ that differ from $u$ at exactly the
positions in $S$ (that is, $v_i \ne u_i$ for $i \in S$ and $v_i = u_i$ for $i \notin S$)
is
\[
  (\abs{\alpha} - 1)^{\abs{S}}.
\]
\end{lemma}

the Hamming distance $d(x,y)$ between two words counts the coordinates in which they
differ. For every radius $k \in \bbn$, the Hamming sphere $S_k(u) = \{v \in \alpha^n :
d(u,v) = k\}$ of words at Hamming distance exactly $k$ from $u$ has cardinality
\[
  \abs{S_k(u)} = \binom{n}{k}\,(\abs{\alpha}-1)^k.
\]
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet, and consider words of length $n$ over $\alpha$. For
any centre word $u \in \alpha^n$ and any radius $r$, the Hamming ball $B_r(u)$ has
cardinality equal to the ball volume at radius $r$ for a length-$n$ code over an
alphabet of size $\abs{\alpha}$; that is,
\[
  \abs{B_r(u)} = \sum_{i=0}^{r} \binom{n}{i}\,(\abs{\alpha} - 1)^i.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Binary ball volume]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.ballVol_binary}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.ballVol_binary}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.ballVol}
\difficulty{1}
For all $n, t \in \bbn$, write $V_q(n,t) = \sum_{i=0}^{t} \binom{n}{i}(q-1)^i$ for the
ball volume at radius $t$ of a length-$n$ code over an alphabet of size $q$. Over a
binary alphabet, i.e. taking $q = 2$, this reduces to the partial sum of binomial
coefficients
\[
  V_2(n,t) = \sum_{i=0}^{t} \binom{n}{i}.
\]
\end{lemma}
